module_title: Advanced Analysis - New Numbering System, Expressways, and Bharatmala
introduction: This advanced level decodes the scientific logic behind the new highway numbering system adopted by India in 2010. We will also analyze the modern 'Expressway' network, monumental tunnels, and the government's flagship Bharatmala Pariyojana.

core_concepts.title: The Scientific Numbering System (2010)
core_concepts.description: India rationalized its highway numbers based on direction and geography. 1. All North-South highways have EVEN numbers (increasing from East to West). 2. All East-West highways have ODD numbers (increasing from North to South). For example, NH-2 is in the East, while NH-68 is in the West. NH-1 is in the North, while NH-87 is in the South.

core_concepts.title: Three-Digit Highways
core_concepts.description: Three-digit numbered highways (e.g., NH-144, NH-244) are secondary routes or branches of the primary one-digit or two-digit parent highway (NH-44). If the first digit is odd, the branch is on the right of the parent; if even, it is on the left.

core_concepts.title: Expressways
core_concepts.description: Expressways are the highest class of roads in India. They are controlled-access highways (6 to 8 lanes) where entry and exit are strictly regulated via ramps, and two-wheelers/tractors are generally banned. 'Uttar Pradesh' has the largest network of operational expressways. The 'Delhi-Mumbai Expressway' will be the longest in India once fully completed.

core_concepts.title: Bharatmala Pariyojana
core_concepts.description: It is an umbrella program for the highways sector that focuses on optimizing efficiency. It replaces the old National Highways Development Project (NHDP). Key components include developing Economic Corridors, Inter Corridors, Feeder Routes, National Corridor Efficiency Improvement, Border and International connectivity roads, and Coastal & Port connectivity roads.

important_entities.name: Dr. Syama Prasad Mookerjee Tunnel (Chenani-Nashri)
important_entities.significance: Located on NH-44 in Jammu and Kashmir, it is over 9 km long and bypasses the snow-bound Patnitop area, reducing the travel time between Jammu and Srinagar by 2 hours.

important_entities.name: Atal Tunnel (Rohtang)
important_entities.significance: Built by the BRO under the Rohtang Pass on the Leh-Manali Highway (Himachal Pradesh). At 9.02 km long, it is a strategic marvel that provides all-weather connectivity to Lahaul-Spiti.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: In Assertion-Reasoning, distinguish between the two. A National Highway is an open-access road with at-grade intersections (crossroads). An Expressway is a closed, 'controlled-access' facility with grade separators (flyovers/underpasses) ensuring uninterrupted high-speed travel.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: If an exam asks to identify an East-West route from a list, immediately eliminate all options with even numbers.

exam_strategy_tips: UPSC occasionally tests the geographical orientation of the new numbering system. Remember: Odd numbers increase from North to South (NH-1 up North, NH-87 down South).
